Case: Todd is a 38-year-old who presents with 6 months of shoulder pain and progressive hand weakness. Todd reports that his pain started after a car accident, and has not improved despite trying ibuprofen, acetaminophen and physical therapy. A steroid injection did relieve some of the pain, but he says this was short-lived and he feels that he is reaching a breaking point with the pain. The neurosurgeon advised that Todd would need an anterior spine surgery, but Todd declined at that time. Repeat CT and MRi of the cervical spine confirm a disc herniation at C4-5 with slight progression in the canal stenosis.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Todd? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
